description: Vector index manifest for the private patient RAG service. Every vector chunk in this index MUST carry the metadata_schema fields below in full. patient_id is the mandatory hard-isolation filter key.

chunking_strategy.fallback_condition: Used only when a source document has no machine-detectable clinical record structure (e.g. unstructured free-text notes, scanned PDFs without OCR-derived section boundaries). Fallback chunks MUST still populate every metadata_schema field; record_type and date may be set to 'unknown' and null respectively when they cannot be determined, and is_multi_event MUST be computed and set to true whenever more than one detectable record boundary falls inside the chunk.

ranking_policy.rule: Similarity ranking alone MUST NOT be trusted for time-sensitive queries (e.g. 'most recent X', 'latest result', 'current dose'). For these, the retriever MUST re-rank the similarity-shortlisted, patient_id-filtered candidates by the date metadata field (descending) before truncating to the context budget.
ranking_policy.rationale: TF-IDF/embedding similarity has no notion of recency: repeated draws of the same lab test are near-equally similar to a 'most recent' query regardless of date. See ai/chunking-experiment.md Section 4 for the experiment that surfaced this.
ranking_policy.dependency: This policy is only reliably enforceable when every chunk carries an accurate, non-null date field, which the selected semantic/document-aware chunking strategy guarantees by construction. The fixed-token fallback strategy cannot reliably support this policy.

isolation_policy.rule: Every query to this index MUST supply a patient_id (or an explicitly authorized set of patient_ids for a delegate/clinician-care-relationship request) BEFORE similarity ranking is performed. The retriever must never rank or return a chunk whose patient_id is not in the caller's authorized set, regardless of similarity score. This is a hard filter, not a re-ranking signal or a post-hoc redaction step.
isolation_policy.consent_check: consent_scope on the chunk must additionally be validated against the caller's authorization (self / delegate / clinician_care_relationship) at query time, per FR-SAN-03 and FR-SAN-05.
isolation_policy.tested_in: ai/chunking-experiment.md (isolation stress test: 0 cross-patient leaks observed across both chunking strategies)

metadata_schema.description: Unique identifier of the patient who owns the underlying record. Mandatory on every chunk; used as the hard isolation/filter key.
Identifier of the source document (medical timeline, lab report, imaging report, etc.) the chunk was extracted from.
Unique identifier of this specific chunk within the document.
Date of the clinical event described in the chunk. If a chunk spans multiple dates (fallback strategy only), the earliest date is stored and is_multi_event is set to true.
Full name of the treating/recording clinician for the event(s) in the chunk.
Type of the clinical record described in the chunk.
Authorization scope required to view this chunk.

True if a single chunk mixes more than one clinical event/record_type. Always false for the selected semantic/document-aware strategy by construction; used as a risk indicator when the fixed-token fallback is used.
Number of tokens in the chunk text, used for token-efficiency accounting and context-budget planning.

notes: Schema field names above are copied verbatim from data-dictionary.csv (System Analyst Data Dictionary placeholder authored alongside this experiment; interns should replace with the authoritative file if/when one is published for the AI repository).

Embedding model for production is not yet selected; this experiment used TF-IDF as a lightweight, offline proxy for retrieval ranking to isolate the effect of chunking strategy. Swapping in a production embedding model does not change the isolation_policy or metadata_schema.
